Best regards,
Chia-Wei

Our school has four bins near the cafeteria for different kinds of waste. Please look carefully before you throw anything away.
The blue bin is for paper only — this means worksheets, notebooks, and cardboard boxes, but not paper with food on it, like a greasy pizza box. The green bin is for plastic bottles and cups; please empty any liquid first and remove the cap before putting it in.

Posted by Ting-Yu, March 3

Last Saturday, my dad and I decided to hike the Qingtiangang trail on Yangmingshan, even though the weather app said it might rain. We packed raincoats just in case, which turned out to be a smart choice!

Last Saturday, my dad and I decided to hike the Qingtiangang trail on Yangmingshan, even though the weather app said it might rain. We packed raincoats just in case, which turned out to be a smart choice!

The mist over the mountains actually made the view look magical, like a scene from a movie.

Learning to Skateboard: My First Month
Posted by Zhi-Hao, June 15

I got my first skateboard as a birthday gift last month, and wow, it has been harder than I expected! In the first week, I couldn't even stand on the board without holding onto a wall. My ankles felt wobbly, and I fell down more times than I can count.

By the second week, I could finally push off and roll a short distance without falling, which felt like a huge win. I watched a lot of videos online to learn the right way to turn and stop safely, since I really didn't want to get hurt.

Now, after a full month of practice almost every day after school, I can ride around the park without holding onto anything, and I'm even starting to learn small jumps called ollies. My knees are covered in small bruises, but I'm honestly proud of how far I've come. Next month, I want to try skating with my friends at the new skate park downtown.

Dear Wei-Ting,

Greetings from Green Island! My family and I arrived two days ago, and I wish you could see how clear the ocean water is here — you can see fish swimming even from the boat. Yesterday, we went snorkeling near a place called Chaikou, and I saw a small sea turtle swimming right below me. I was so surprised that I forgot to breathe through my snorkel for a second!

This morning, we rented bikes and rode around the whole island, which only took about two hours since the island is quite small. We stopped at a hot spring by the sea, which is apparently one of very few saltwater hot springs in the world. Tonight, we're going to try the local flying fish dishes at a night market near our hotel.

We're heading back to Taitung tomorrow afternoon, and then home the next day. I'll show you all my underwater photos when I get back!

Miss you,
Jia-Yun
